units.function: Large mixed unit specification for execution environment/secret layering, low-trust credential gates, Codex-local authentication preflight, run-scoped Skill mentions, referenced-project authorization/synchronization/observability, workspace hints and managed project directory isolation.
units.dependencyDirection: Heartbeat orchestration combines Secret service resolution, trust preset and responsible user context, adapter-specific credential checks, Skill mention parsing/sync config, authorization decisions, Project/workspace lookup, managed clone helpers and filesystem paths before passing a composite adapter configuration and workspace hints to execution.
units.keyDataModels: Environment/Agent/Project/Routine env layers and secret manifest, user/company secret binding and responsibleUserId, low-trust allowed binding IDs, required scoped env key preflight, Codex home/API-key auth, run-scoped desired Skill/version pin, project:read authorization, referenced-project sync warning/failure counts, additional workspace/hint and Company/Project managed path.
units.lifecycle: Environment, Agent, Project and Routine env are resolved with later layers overriding earlier values and secret IDs unioned; PAPERCLIP_API_KEY bindings are dropped while other PAPERCLIP-prefixed names remain; required user bindings fail before resolution and low-trust inline sensitive values are rejected/allowlisted; Git push checks for named credentials at Agent/Project scope; local Codex checks per-Agent API key or shared host subscription auth but sandbox targets skip the host gate; mentioned Skills are deduplicated and appended; authorized referenced Projects are resolved independently, failures warn while remaining work continues, remote targets drop all local staging, and valid configured/managed workspaces become adapter path hints in isolated sibling directories.
units.testAssessment: Thirty-five tests cover precedence, secret manifests, reserved-key stripping, absent layers, low-trust binding propagation, required user secrets, inline sensitive denial, push key presence, Codex local/sandbox/shared auth, Skill ID/version behavior, referenced-project feature gating/authorization/partial failures/remote staging/observability/hints, missing/empty workspace sources, managed clone fallback and path non-nesting. Missing are real Secret/authorization/database/filesystem integration across most helpers; mutation/override authorization; semantic env schemas and future reserved-name collisions; secret TTL/audience/permission verification; Git token repository/write scope; sandbox credential provenance; cross-Company shared Codex auth isolation; data classification/export and mandatory-versus-optional referenced inputs; repo ref checkout/integrity; symlink/path traversal; workspace remote verification; Skill trust/signature/capability authorization; failure policy and immutable selection/evidence receipts.
units.designRationale: Centralize run preparation so configuration is deterministic and inspectable, resolve secrets only at execution time, constrain low-trust runs, fail early on missing credentials, allow optional cross-project context without making one clone failure fatal, and prevent managed Project directories from nesting or colliding.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs enterprise data authorization and export control across layered configuration, human-owned secrets, tools/Skills and multiple project data sources, while supporting cloud/local execution without leaking vendor credentials or silently changing Work semantics.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT as separate canonical components, not one Heartbeat helper: ConfigurationPolicy resolves typed non-secret settings; CredentialBrokerPort issues short-lived action/resource-scoped capabilities and secret-free manifests; DataAuthorizationContract classifies each required/optional source and egress; Tool/Skill capability admission verifies publisher/version/signature; WorkspacePort stages content-addressed sources and attestations. Preserve deterministic precedence, pre-resolution missing-binding checks, low-trust allowlists, structured partial-failure observability and non-nested paths. Replace key-name presence with verified provider capabilities, forbid inline secrets at every trust level, reserve an explicit namespace, isolate all user/provider auth per Company, and require the Work policy to choose fail-closed versus optional continuation for missing referenced Projects.
units.responsibilityConflict: responsibleUserId appears only in missing-secret diagnostics and does not approve environment precedence, shared host authentication, Git write access, Skills or additional Project disclosure. A plaintext GH_TOKEN can satisfy push preflight without proving scope; sandbox credentials are assumed; shared Codex auth may fund or identify multiple Companies; partial project loss still executes; local cwd/repository hints enter Agent context without an immutable data contract. These are configuration conveniences, not a complete responsibility/evidence chain.
